references.text: The journey from Mount Hor is mentioned here, where Aaron died. This is the starting point for the journey described in Num 21:4.
The first time the Israelites are told to head toward the Red Sea (Sea of Reeds) as a detour.
Parallel account that Israel turned toward the Red Sea to go around Edom.
Edom refused to let Israel pass through their land, which led them to go around the territory of Edom.
The expression 'קְצַר רוּחַ' (short of spirit/impatient) is used to describe the people's discouragement, similar to 'וַתִּקְצַר נֶפֶשׁ' in our text.
The same expression 'וַתִּקְצַר נַפְשׁוֹ' is used regarding the Lord's impatience with Israel's suffering.
The expression 'וַתִּקְצַר נַפְשׁוֹ' is used concerning Samson, whose soul became impatient.
The route from Mount Hor is mentioned in the camp records.
The New Testament refers to those who sinned in the wilderness and how God became angry with the people during their journey.
Paul warns against complaining as the Israelites did in the wilderness, referencing events in 4 Mosebok.
